doc:
**Goal.** The reference for telling oaks and their hybrids apart, in Jeff's words, every claim traceable to its source. Done when taxa live in the new model linked to iNat; Jeff's material is in the database, private; facts are sourced and reviewable with Jeff's leading; Jeff writes and publishes entries in the site; the public site runs on the new design (taxon pages, comparisons, ID tool); every data change goes through the app or the import endpoint.

**Appetite.** About 6 weeks from now, scope cut rather than slipped. At most 3 agents, on disjoint areas; Taxonomy and Material can run side by side.

**Rules it adds.** R7 (contexts; its check comes with the first item), R9, R21, R26, R27.

**Settled (don't reopen).** SQLite. No audit log, no undo. iNat is the backbone; North America first. Varieties are taxa. Agents work outside the app; the app makes no LLM calls. Facts from Jeff's writing are proposed with the quote and count only when he accepts. The editor is in the site. Entries: key sentence, account, historical context, more later. No bulk iNat exports. One taxon template; comparisons at `?vs=`, the reader at `?read=`. Facts aren't copyrightable; Jeff's prose is. Any source can supply range data. ID mode starts as a feature list plus a link. The book is out of scope. No API key rotation for now. Design references: PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, design/prototype/, .impeccable/surfaces/; UI work uses the impeccable skill at medium and large size.

**Order.** Polish, then Sources and facts core; Taxonomy and Material side by side; then Traits and fact review, Authoring editor, Taxon pages, ID tool, Ranges and maps. Each phase's doc has its done-when and outline.

**Goal.** The two remaining ports from gallformers: the code-review command (a518) and structured JSON logging in prod (ba39). **Appetite.** 1 day. **Rules it adds.** None. **Phase** Ports (c3b2), done when both are accepted; then close the plan.

**Goal.** Search covers names, published entry sections and facts, and stays fast as content grows. **Appetite.** 1 week, after Taxon pages. **Rules it adds.** None new (R10 holds).

**To settle when shaping** (these replace questions e821 and 3bff): coverage is names, published entry sections and facts, through SQLite FTS5; results stay grouped by kind, with ranking inside a group only if FTS5's bm25 is enough. First, bug 4742 (search broken): confirm it still reproduces. Idea fa45 (say which common name matched) joins. Phases are cut when Jeff agrees the plan.

Appetite: 3 days.

Done when:
- Jeff calls the site acceptable on desktop and phone
- check-ui passes
- R17's ratchet is at most 12.

Appetite: 3 days.

Done when:
- a fact stores with its sources, evidence and standing
- Jeff's fact leads its slot in a test
- a disagreement raises a conflict in a test
- a read model returns a taxon's facts per slot
- `mix compile` enforces Boundary.

Appetite: 5 days.

Done when:
- every species row is a taxon with names, loaded through the import after Jeff read the dry-run report
- hybrids have sourced parentage
- varieties and subspecies are child taxa with a stored rank
- taxa carry iNat ids
- today's pages and v1 API tests pass through the adapter.

Outline (cut into items when the phase starts): taxa, names and ancestry (port gallformers' Ancestry, tree validator, NameNormalizer); hybrids and parentage; migrate species (fixing bugs b558, cb93, a946); iNat sync; editorial fields; adapter. Idea ed7a.

Appetite: 3 days, beside Taxonomy.

Done when:
- compendium-notes is loaded after Jeff's sample check
- a test shows no public route returns materials
- duplicates are grouped
- Jeff can capture one iNat comment or observation by URL.

Outline (cut into items when the phase starts): materials schema; load compendium-notes; duplicate grouping; observations and capture.

Appetite: 5 days.

Done when:
- Jeff approved the vocabulary
- counts and other sources' values are facts
- an agent can propose a fact with its quote through the import
- Jeff can accept, edit or decline it and resolve conflicts (prototypes ed-facts, ed-conflicts).

Outline (cut into items when the phase starts): vocabulary; load measures and source facts; proposals; review screen; conflicts screen.

Appetite: 5 days.

Done when:
- Jeff opens a taxon, sees text marked by provenance, inserts material verbatim, marks sections written and publishes them
- a test shows the import refuses entry text (R21 gets its check).

Outline (cut into items when the phase starts): entry structure (ask da8b); entries, versions and provenance; editor screen; load the live short text for review; publishing (ask 7570); a section across taxa.

All UI work uses the impeccable skill, with its finish review; design input is in design/prototype/ and .impeccable/surfaces/.

Appetite: 5 days.

Done when:
- species, hybrid, variety and higher taxa pages use one template on real data
- `?vs=` and `?read=` work
- Impeccable's finish review passes.

Outline (cut into items when the phase starts): first, the components the page needs, in the library (ideas 334d, 45f6); taxon page; comparison mode; hybrid and infraspecific pages; browse, species list and sources pages; API caching plug. Queue: d2a4, 180f. Ideas a41d, 4533.

All UI work uses the impeccable skill, with its finish review; design input is in design/prototype/ and .impeccable/surfaces/.

Appetite: 5 days.

Done when:
- the trait filter and hybrid helper work on real North American facts with range overlap and hedging
- ID mode copies a comment for an observation.

Outline (cut into items when the phase starts): matching engine; trait filter; hybrid helper; ID mode. Ideas c948, a903.

All UI work uses the impeccable skill, with its finish review; design input is in design/prototype/ and .impeccable/surfaces/.

Appetite: 3 days.

Done when:
- taxa have sourced range facts per place and the taxon page draws a map from them.

Outline (cut into items when the phase starts): boundary data; range facts; map component (in the library); map on the page.

text: Two fixes to your article How to Document an Oak: a "- " before "vestiture" (review 3ff5) and *...* around its scientific names (bug ba9a). They change no words, but it is your text.
default: You make them in the article editor; no agent touches it.

text: Publishing: does marking a section written publish it, or do sections wait for a Publish?
default: Marking a section written publishes it.

text: Entry structure: which sections follow key sentence, account and historical context?
default: Those three for now; more are added as you need them.
